intervention: model class: developmental hypomyelination (WWOX neuron-deleted, E01-E08)
effect_note: Reference class for the comparison: deficit arises during the first postnatal weeks, before the adult state; reconnaissance row E01-E08 and E13-E16 hold the numbers.
transfer_conditions: External system pertinent only if the deficit arises during primary myelination (mouse ~P7-P21), the perturbation is present from the start, and an OPC-to-oligodendrocyte maturation step is read.
transfer_breakers: Injury or toxic models (cuprizone, lysolecithin, EAE) start from a normally myelinated, mature tract; the repair programme (existing OPC pool, inflammatory milieu) differs from first-time myelination.

intervention: model class: toxic demyelination then remyelination (cuprizone, E26)
system: mouse Olig2-Cre WWOX deletion, adult, cuprizone
effect_note: Primary oligodendroglial WWOX role appears only under this challenge, in an unreviewed preprint; OPC accumulation with fewer CC1+ cells in recovery (E26, N=2-3).
transfer_conditions: Shows that the same gene can matter to the lineage under injury; OPC differentiation block reading is shared with developmental screens.
transfer_breakers: Adult injury-repair is not developmental hypomyelination; WWOX Olig2-Cre deletion gives no developmental hypomyelination (E10). A remyelination hit cannot be carried to the neonatal setting without a developmental test.

effect_note: Ageing phenotype in the lineage-restricted deletion is a late challenge phenotype, preprint only.
transfer_conditions: Pertinent only for a late-onset oligodendroglial component.
transfer_breakers: Ageing myelin loss has a different driver and different OPC state; it does not model a neonatal deficit.

cell_type_or_stage: neuron-restricted deletion and add-back; OL lineage deletion
control: Olig2-Cre deletion no major MBP change (E10); neuron add-back restores EM counts and g-ratio with OL lineage still null (E13-E16)
effect_note: Driver is upstream of the oligodendrocyte (IT14 P4 RESTRICT); one seizure-free co-culture (E09: wild-type OPCs on null DRG neurons, myelinating share ~49 v 29 percent, n=4 v 4) and one preprint OPC monoculture (E23). Mediator unknown.
transfer_conditions: An external system shares the driver only if the OL deficit follows a neuronal or axonal defect and the OL is genetically intact. A pro-differentiation intervention is pertinent only if it acts downstream of the missing neuronal signal.
transfer_breakers: Most external pro-differentiation systems (OPC screens, OPC-restricted knockouts) have an oligodendrocyte-intrinsic or autocrine defect; the missing neuronal signal in WWOX could be absent in the dish and a pro-differentiation agent may not substitute for it.

intervention: model class: oligodendrocyte-intrinsic postnatal OPC deletion (Pdk1 icKO) treated with a promyelinating drug
stress_or_context: deletion induced at P10-P12, no seizures reported
effect_note: Drug restored oligodendrogenesis, myelin area and Y-maze alternation in mutants; treatment started after deletion, in a lineage-intrinsic defect. Pdk1 pathway not a WWOX partner.
locator_quote: spontaneous alternation rates were significantly increased in clemastine-treated Pdk1 icKO mice compared to saline-treated mutants
transfer_conditions: Developmental postnatal hypomyelination with a behavioural readout (memory), no demyelination step; a functional rescue by differentiation enhancement is possible in principle.
transfer_breakers: Driver is oligodendrocyte-intrinsic, not neuronal; no seizures, no survival crisis; memory tests need an animal that survives and moves; no conduction or EM compaction readout after treatment read; effect attribution to the target of the drug is not tested (compound_only).

intervention: model class: neuroligin-3 mutant hypomyelination treated with a promyelinating drug
system: mouse NL3-R451C KI and OPC-NL3 cKO, barrel cortex
control: vehicle-treated KI; OPC-NL3 cKO phenocopy; Myrf cKO myelination block
effect_note: Promyelinating drug restored PV-interneuron myelination, excitability and texture discrimination; OPC-restricted NL3 deletion phenocopies, so the driver is at least partly oligodendroglial, not simply neuronal.
transfer_conditions: Closest external case in which hypomyelination is linked to a neurodevelopmental gene and a functional (sensory behaviour, oscillation) readout rescued.
transfer_breakers: Adult treatment at P60; autism-class model without seizures; the OPC-specific cKO shows an intrinsic arm, which weakens the analogy with a neuron-driven WWOX deficit; compound_only attribution.

intervention: model class: oligodendrocyte maturation defect with epilepsy susceptibility (Adamts4 KO, Myrf cKO) treated with a promyelinating drug
effect_note: Drug given in the early postnatal period rescued mossy-fibre development and attenuated adult epilepsy susceptibility; Myrf cKO (maturation block) itself caused spontaneous seizures and death, so the OL maturation defect can drive seizures rather than follow them.
locator_quote: enhancing differentiation by orally administered clemastine rescues the defective mossy fiber development in the early postnatal period and attenuates epilepsy susceptibility in adults
transfer_conditions: Only external case where a pro-differentiation drug given in a developmental window changes a seizure-related functional outcome; the neonatal window matches WWOX add-back (P0-P5).
transfer_breakers: Mild genetic OL differentiation defect, not a neuronal-gene DEE; seizure susceptibility to a chemoconvulsant in adults, not spontaneous DEE seizures; reverse arrow (OL defect causes seizures) is opposite to the WWOX neuron-first reading.

intervention: model class: neonatal hypoxia-ischaemia injury treated with a promyelinating drug
effect_note: Treatment after injury ameliorated adolescent sociability deficit and hypomyelination; read from abstract only.
locator_quote: clemastine successfully ameliorated HI-induced social deficits during adolescence, attenuated hypomyelination and promoted oligodendrocyte maturation
transfer_breakers: Injury model with OPC loss and debris; not a genetic or neuron-driven deficit; abstract only.

intervention: model class: gain-of-function sodium channel DEE (Scn2a A263V) with spontaneous neonatal seizures
effect_note: Neuronal hyperexcitability in a DEE model gave slightly faster conduction and increased grey-matter myelination, no loss of CC1+ cells: the direction is opposite to WWOX hypomyelination, so seizure activity alone does not predict hypomyelination (activity-dependent adaptation).
locator_quote: the enhanced myelination likely reflects an activity-dependent adaptation to altered neuronal network activity rather than a primary myelinopathy
transfer_conditions: Tests whether seizure-bearing DEE per se reduces myelin: here it did not, which lowers (does not remove) the seizure-secondary explanation of WWOX hypomyelination.
transfer_breakers: Different gene and channel mechanism (gain of excitability); WWOX null also has metabolic illness and early death; one gene's result does not transfer to another.

intervention: model class: compensatory myelination of inhibitory axons (Gabrd KO) with promyelinating drug phenocopy
system: mouse hippocampus, PV interneuron maturation window
effect_note: Myelination gain is protective against seizures in this window and absent in an adult-acquired model; abstract of a non-peer-reviewed preprint.
locator_quote: Pharmacological reinforcement of myelination with clemastine during PV+ interneuron maturation phenocopied the seizure-resistant state
transfer_conditions: Illustrates that the sign of a pro-myelination effect on seizure threshold can be favourable in a defined window.
transfer_breakers: Preprint, abstract only; more myelin is the intended exposure in Gabrd, not a rescue of a deficit; a pro-differentiation drug could be beneficial or not for the same endpoint depending on the circuit.

intervention: model class: human WWOX developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, imaging
system: patients, MRI (mini-review of case series including 13 patients)
effect_note: Atrophy (13 of 13 in one series) and corpus callosum hypoplasia (12 of 13) dominate; delayed myelination in a minority (6 of 13) with progression on serial MRI. Endpoint is therefore atrophy/callosal and delayed myelination, not hypomyelination as a leukodystrophy.
locator_quote: they also reported delayed myelination and white matter hyperintense signals
transfer_conditions: A comparison is pertinent for the callosal and myelination-delay components; MRI is a population-level marker.
transfer_breakers: MRI cannot separate hypomyelination, delayed myelination, loss and axonal atrophy; case series are small and heterogeneous; a myelin endpoint may not be the dominant human lesion (see E31).

intervention: model class: myelination window, rodent versus human
cell_type_or_stage: preoligodendrocyte to immature OL; myelination peak
effect_note: Rodent pnd 1-3 corresponds to 23-32 weeks of human gestation, pnd 7 to 32-36 weeks, pnd 10 to term; rodent myelination is well under way by pnd 10-14 and peaks near pnd 20; human white matter keeps growing into the third decade.
transfer_conditions: The WWOX add-back window (P0-P5) corresponds to the human late-gestation window, before term; a screen that tests differentiation in P0-P7 OPCs or P10-P20 myelination matches the mouse endpoint.
transfer_breakers: Human infants with WWOX-DEE are seen after term, at stages whose mouse equivalent is P10-P20 or later; whether a late-gestation window can be targeted in humans is unaddressed; the equivalence is regional, not global.

intervention: model class: readout dissociation, structural marker versus function
system: mouse Pdk1 icKO and Scn2a A263V
effect_note: Pdk1 icKO had thinner but normally compacted myelin; Scn2a mutant had altered oligodendroglial maturation transcripts with only slightly faster conduction and unchanged CC1 counts; a marker change (MBP, CC1, transcript) does not fix myelin compaction or conduction.
locator_quote: Ultrastructural examination revealed normally compacted myelin sheaths without overt dysmorphic features in Pdk1 icKO mice
transfer_conditions: A transfer row should state the level at which the external perturbation was read (transcript, immunostaining, EM, conduction, behaviour).
transfer_breakers: WWOX numbers are mostly immunofluorescence intensity over sections (E01, pseudoreplication) and an Mbp transcript share (0.30); no conduction or EM at P17 for the external comparison.

intervention: model class: pro-differentiation intervention improving a function in a seizure-bearing neuron-driven hypomyelination model
effect_note: No source found in which a pro-differentiation intervention improved a conduction, motor, seizure or behavioural outcome in a model where hypomyelination follows a neuronal defect and seizures are present; positive functional rescues (rows C05-C08) come from oligodendrocyte-intrinsic, injury or seizure-free models. Search was a Europe PMC query set, not exhaustive.
transfer_conditions: An absence in a bounded search; not evidence of no effect.
transfer_breakers: Would reopen with a screen of Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like, Scn1a/Scn2a/Kcnq2 and Stxbp1 models with a myelin-promoting arm and electrophysiology.
